title: Keeping Your Own Soul While Feeding Others
subtitle: How a pastor guards his own walk with God against the professionalized faith problem, where Scripture becomes raw material and prayer becomes preparation and the leader slowly starves at the banquet he serves.

sections.title: The Cook Can Starve in a Full Kitchen
sections.body:
There is a danger built into this work that no other Christian faces in quite the same way. Your relationship with God is also your job. The Word you live by is the Word you process for a paycheck. The prayer that should be your breath is also a duty on your calendar. And slowly, without ever deciding to, you can stop eating the food you spend all week preparing.

The cook can starve in a full kitchen. The man surrounded by the things of God can grow cold to the God of those things, because familiarity dulls and handling holy things every day can make a man forget they are holy at all.

This is not a small risk. It is the occupational hazard of the calling, and most pastors who lose their souls do not lose them in scandal. They lose them in routine.

sections.title: When Scripture Becomes Raw Material
sections.body:
Watch how it happens. You open the Bible and your first question is no longer what is God saying to me. It is what can I do with this on Sunday. The text stops being food and becomes inventory. You read it the way a contractor reads a lumber yard, scanning for usable pieces, and the part of you that once trembled at the Word goes quiet.

Prayer goes the same way. It becomes preparation instead of communion. You pray about the service, the meeting, the people, and you never simply come to be with the Father as a son. Your faith gets professionalized. It becomes a competence you perform rather than a life you live.

The verdict is brutal in its quietness. A man can become an expert in God and a stranger to Him in the same career.

sections.title: Read for Your Soul Before You Read for the Sermon
sections.body:
The remedy is not complicated, but it costs time you feel you do not have. You must come to God for yourself before you come to Him for the church. There must be Scripture you read with no pen in your hand, no sermon forming, no outline taking shape. Just a hungry man at the table, eating.

Robert Murray McCheyne said the greatest need of his people was his own personal holiness. He was right. The flock is fed first by what feeds the shepherd. If you are not being nourished, you will eventually serve them leftovers, reheated, lifeless, the form of food without its life.

Guard a private walk that has nothing to do with your public work. It is not selfish. It is the source. Dry up there and everything downstream dries up with you.

sections.title: Pay Closest Attention to Yourself
sections.body:
Paul told the Ephesian elders to pay careful attention to themselves first, and then to the flock. The order is not an accident. The man who watches everyone else and stops watching himself is the man most likely to fall, because he has aimed all his vigilance outward and left his own door unguarded.

Keeping your soul means watching your soul. Asking the hard questions. Am I tender or am I just busy. Do I still love Him or do I only work for Him. When did I last weep over my own sin instead of only naming everyone else's. The honest answers are uncomfortable, and that discomfort is a mercy, because it means the watchman is still awake.

Watch yourself. The soul you are most responsible for, and the one you are most tempted to neglect, is your own.

sections.title: Do Not Die at the Banquet You Serve
sections.body:
It is possible to spend a lifetime ushering people to the feast and never sit down to eat. To talk of grace and grow hard. To preach about the love of God on Sunday and not have felt it yourself in months. To hand out bread with starving hands.

Do not let it be you. The same Christ you offer to the people is offered to you, freely, today, as a son and not a servant. Come and eat first. A fed shepherd feeds the flock. A starving one only performs.

Keep your own soul. Everything else you have to give depends on it.
